stories.headline: Valles Marineris flood may have raised ancient Martian sea level by 34 metres
stories.title: Valles Marineris flood may have raised ancient Martian sea level by 34 metres
stories.summary: The flood, from the ancient canyon system, the largest in the Solar System, is estimated to have released 1,245 trillion cubic metres of water and may have raised the global mean level of the hypothesised ancient Martian ocean by about 34 metres, according to a new study published online in the peer-reviewed journal Icarus.

article_sentences: The recent catastrophic flash floods in Nepal, apparently triggered by the collapse of a glacier rock mass that sent ice, rock, and sediment downstream, causing a sudden surge of water and debris in the river, highlight the destructive power of such events.
A vastly larger outburst flood occurred on Mars, where the breaching of paleolakes in Valles Marineris during the Late Hesperian to Early Amazonian unleashed a massive deluge.

The flood, from the ancient canyon system, the largest in the Solar System, is estimated to have released 1,245 trillion cubic metres of water and may have raised the global mean level of the hypothesised ancient Martian ocean by about 34 metres, according to a new study published online in the peer-reviewed journal Icarus.
The researchers estimate that an equivalent discharge on Earth would have inundated about 3.6 million sq km of land.

The study was conducted by Sajin Kumar, assistant professor in the Department of Geology, University of Kerala, and his team, along with researchers from the Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology, Okayama University in Japan, and the University of Mississippi and Michigan State University, both in the United States.
The researchers used two-dimensional hydraulic modelling to reconstruct the flood and assess its impact on the hypothesised ancient Martian ocean.

According to the researchers, the principal breach occurred at Eos Chasma, where the Valles Marineris trough connects eastward to Aurorae chaos, releasing an estimated 1,245 trillion cubic metres of water.

Smaller breaches were modelled at Daga Vallis and Columbia Valles, with the floodwaters routed through Chryse Planitia before ultimately reaching the northern lowlands and the hypothesised ancient ocean known as Oceanus Borealis.
In addition to the estimated global mean rise, the hydraulic modelling showed the sudden discharge would have produced a local transient rise of 324 metres at the outflow terminus.
Valles Marineris stretches more than 4,000 km across Mars’s equatorial region and is thought to have once contained extensive bodies of water, including paleolakes.
Researchers estimate that these waterbodies contained about 2,369 trillion cubic metres, with simulations suggesting that roughly half was released during the catastrophic breach.
Mr. Kumar said an equivalent discharge on Earth would have severe global consequences.

stories.headline: Terrorist killed in AshdarGali encounter: Army
stories.title: Terrorist killed in AshdarGali encounter: Army
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sep 4: Army on Friday said that one terrorist was killed in a joint operation with J&K Police and CRPF in AshdarGali in central district of Budgam they have recovered an AK rifle along with other war-like stores. The operation is underway and more reinforcements has been sent to the area. The Srinagar-based Chinar Corps of the Indian Army, in a post on X, said the operation, named OP ASHDAR, was launched jointly by the Army, J&K Police, and CRPF Srinagar Sector in the general area of AshdarGali after specific intelligence inputs. “Vigilant troops observed suspicious activity and upon being challenged, terrorists opened fire, prompting a fierce exchange of gunfire during which one terrorist was neutralised and one AK rifle and other war-like stores recovered. Search operation is in progress,” the Corps said. Officials said the operation began on Thursday evening after intelligence about the movement of terrorists in the area. They said contact was established when troops challenged the terrorists opened fire first. "One terrorist was killed in the ensuing gunfight. Identity of the slain terrorist has not been established so far. Additional forces have been rushed to strengthen the cordon," officials said. AshdarGali is a remote, high-altitude forested mountain pass in the central valley ridge of the PirPanjal range. It sits on the rugged highland corridor linking Pakherpora in Pulwama with Yousmarg in Budgam and has historically served as a secluded transit route across district boundaries. The steep ridges and thick forest cover make movement difficult to detect and operations challenging. The two-day encounter comes after a prolonged lull in armed clashes in Kashmir. The last confirmed major gunfight in the Valley was in Shopian in July. The action follows heightened operational focus on the same mountain belt. Sixteen days earlier, on August 19, Director General of Police Nalin Prabhat, accompanied by the then Inspector General of Police Kashmir Zone V K Birdi and DIG Central Kashmir Range Rajiv Pandey, along with SSP Budgam Hariprasad K K, conducted an operational review of Temporary Operating Bases on the northern face of the Pir Panjal, including the Todasmaidan sector.

stories.headline: Imran Ansari meets Iranian Chief Justice during New Delhi visit
stories.title: Imran Ansari meets Iranian Chief Justice during New Delhi visit
stories.summary: President of the All Jammu and Kashmir Shia Association and JKPC General Secretary, Molvi Imran Ansari, met the Chief Justice of the Islamic Republic of Iran, Ayatollah Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Eje’i, during his official visit to New Delhi for the BRICS judicial leaders’ summit. The meeting was also attended by Dr. Mohammad Fathali, Ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to India, and Dr. Abdul Majid Hakeem Ilahi, Representative of the Supreme Leader of Iran in India. During the interaction, Molvi Imran Ansari conveyed his respect for the people of Iran and remembered the martyrs of Iran, including Ayatollah Sayyid Ali Hosseini Khamenei, as well as the innocent victims of the tragic Minab school incident, particularly the children. He offered prayers for the departed and expressed solidarity with their families. Speaking about Kashmir’s historic relationship with Iran, Molvi Imran Ansari said that the connection between the two societies goes back centuries and is deeply rooted in civilization rather than politics alone. Persian language and literature, Islamic scholarship, poetry, architecture, art and traditional crafts have all played an important role in shaping Kashmir’s cultural and intellectual heritage. For generations, scholars and ideas travelled between these regions, creating a relationship of faith, knowledge and mutual respect. Molvi Imran Ansari also spoke about the historic relationship between India and Iran, describing the two countries as ancient civilizations connected through centuries of cultural exchange, trade and people-to-people relations. (KNS)

stories.headline: Tata Motors turns to Iveco shareholders to seal €3.82-billion takeover
stories.title: Tata Motors turns to Iveco shareholders to seal €3.82-billion takeover
stories.summary: With regulators cleared and financing secured, the Italian truck maker’s investors now hold the key to determining the deal’s outcome
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Tata Motors has cleared regulatory hurdles and lined up the financing for its €3.82-billion takeover of Iveco Group.
Its final challenge is the company’s shareholders.
In a regulatory filing in the early hours of September 5, Tata laid out the shareholder arithmetic that will determine whether it can take control of the Italian truck maker.
Exor, Iveco’s largest shareholder, has committed its 27.06% stake to Tata’s offer.
The rest will be decided when the €14.10-a-share tender opens on September 7.
“The commencement of the tender offer marks an important milestone,” Tata Motors Managing Director and CEO Girish Wagh said.

By combining the companies’ strengths, capabilities and market presence, he said, Tata has the opportunity to build “a stronger, more globally competitive commercial vehicle business” that can invest in future technologies and create sustainable value.
“We believe the tender offer presents a compelling value proposition for Iveco Group shareholders,” Wagh said.
The latest filing follows Tata’s September 4 disclosure that the Italian securities regulator, CONSOB, had approved the offer document on September 3, clearing the way for the shareholder tender.
That followed sector authorisation from the European Central Bank on September 1, meaning all required competition, foreign investment, foreign subsidy, and regulatory approvals have been obtained.
Tata enters the shareholder phase with several factors in its favour.
Iveco’s board has unanimously recommended the offer, while Exor has irrevocably committed its 27.06% holding and agreed to vote in favour of all transaction-related resolutions.

stories.headline: Kashmir records 25% rain deficit in August
stories.title: Kashmir records 25% rain deficit in August
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sep 4: Kashmir recorded a 25 percent rainfall deficit in August, while the Jammu division remained normal at minus 16 percent and Ladakh recorded a 2 percent surplus, according to India Meteorological Department (IMD) data. Kashmir received 615.2 mm of rain against a normal of 815.5 mm, while Jammu received 2,452.9 mm against a normal of 2,930.7 mm. Jammu’s 16 percent deficit was within the normal range. Under IMD classification, rainfall departure between minus 19 percent and 19 percent is normal, minus 20 percent to minus 59 percent is deficit, below minus 60 percent is large deficit, 20 percent to 59 percent is excess and 60 percent or more is large excess. Rainfall varied sharply across districts and locations. Higher reaches in several districts across JK recorded intense showers and occasional cloudbursts, while lower areas generally received light to moderate spells. Some intense spells triggered flash floods, landslides, mudslides, shooting stones, rockfalls and heavy runoff. KASHMIR SEES WIDE VARIATIONS Shopian recorded the highest deficit at minus 57 percent, followed by Budgamat minus 50 percent and Anantnag at minus 39 percent. Kupwara was minus 36 percent below normal and Baramulla was minus 33 percent. Kulgam and Srinagar were normal at minus 14 percent and minus 13 percent. Ganderbal and Budgam were also normal at minus 9 percent and minus 3 percent each. Pulwama was the only Kashmir district to record excess rainfall, at 24 percent, receiving 90 mm against a normal of 72.7 mm. JAMMU DISTRICTS DIVERGE Kishtwar recorded a large deficit of minus 78 percent, followed by Rajouri at minus 55 percent, Jammu at minus 38 percent, Reasi at minus 36 percent, and Ramban at minus 28 percent. Poonch recorded excess rainfall at 21 percent. Udhampur and Samba stood normal at minus 17 percent and minus 9 percent while Kathua and Doda were surplus at 4 percent each. LADAKH RECORDS SURPLUS Ladakh recorded a 2 percent surplus, within the normal category. Leh received 19.8 mm against a normal of 5.6 mm, a large excess of 253 percent, while Kargil received 10.3 mm against a normal of 9 mm, a 15 percent surplus. Earlier, June recorded a minus 24 percent deficit, with J&K receiving 57.9 mm against a normal of 75.9 mm. July reversed the trend, with J&K and Ladakh receiving 259.7 mm against a normal of 192.6 mm, a 35 percent excess. The July gain offset the June and August deficits, leaving June-August summer rainfall in the normal category across Jammu and Kashmir. Rainfall had also remained deficient in spring, with J&K recording a 28 percent deficit from March through May. Kashmir was 36 percent below normal, Jammu 20 percent below normal. However, Ladakh was surplus at 26 percent.

stories.headline: India’s 7.8% GDP: A moment for confidence with candour
stories.title: India’s 7.8% GDP: A moment for confidence with candour
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: More than two thousand years ago, Kautilya understood a principle that modern economics continues to rediscover: the ultimate test of statecraft is not the splendour of statistics, but the welfare of the people.
India’s latest GDP numbers, therefore, deserve both celebration and scrutiny.
The economy has scored an impressive 7.8% in the first quarter of 2026-27, beating the Reserve Bank of India’s 7% expectation and the market consensus of around 7.1%.
Manufacturing grew 9.2%, financial services 12.1%, private investment accelerated sharply and private consumption remained resilient.
They suggest that, despite geopolitical turbulence, expensive energy, uncertain global trade and a difficult external environment, India’s domestic economic engine remains remarkably resilient.
For a country aspiring to become Viksit Bharat by 2047, this is no small achievement.
But economics is rarely as simple as a headline number.
The controversy surrounding the GDP figure has acquired an unnecessary political colour.
Supporters of the Government have treated the number as evidence of India’s economic success, while critics have questioned whether the methodology captures the economy’s true pulse.
Both sides deserve to be heard.
The government’s case is technically strong on one important point.
India has recently shifted its GDP series from the 2011-12 base year to 2022-23, incorporating newer data sources and a substantially more detailed system of price deflators.
